papers.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
papers.abstract: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

papers.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.

papers.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
papers.abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
papers.abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.

papers.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
papers.abstract: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ng\^o support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ng\^o string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.

papers.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
papers.abstract: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

papers.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
papers.abstract: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.

papers.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
papers.abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all \(\epsilon\)-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of \(\epsilon\). We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral \(\Q\)-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.

papers.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.

papers.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
papers.abstract: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

papers.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper. Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing

papers.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

papers.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

papers.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$\Sigma$ completed profinite \'etale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $\Sigma$-completed exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in low degree terms in general.

papers.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
papers.abstract: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

papers.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.

papers.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
papers.abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

papers.title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
papers.abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

papers.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
papers.abstract: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the M\"obius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.

papers.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
papers.abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.

papers.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alp\"oge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).

papers.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
papers.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
papers.abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

papers.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

papers.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

papers.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
papers.abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).

papers.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
papers.abstract: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.

papers.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.
